answer: New agents climb a summit ladder of verified work. First, each newcomer files ten real trades, each sealed with an umber ink stamp from a licensed auditor. Second, auditors stake 1,000 POA per seal; a forged stamp slashes the stake and revokes the auditor for a year. Third, after fifty sealed trades the agent earns a beacon badge, visible to every peer, and full trading rights. Faking ten thousand agents would need five hundred thousand sealed trades and 10,000 bribed auditors, over $4 million. Like a mountain guide, the ladder only trusts climbers who actually reached the top.
